name: Reel Viewer
description: A pocket picture theatre. Insert a circular reel, pull the little lever, and peer into original illustrated places, miniature worlds and photographs.

assets.credit: Original Elsewhere toy and illustrated miniature worlds

compatibility: Canvas 2D and CSS; no WebGL or third-party runtime. ResizeObserver, Pointer Events, modern Safari, Chrome and Firefox. A static original toy illustration remains without JavaScript.
Keyboard arrows, large previous/next buttons, clickable reel frames, and horizontal touch swipes. Captions and image descriptions remain real accessible text.

Parallel stereo uses separate off-axis viewpoints. Viewing fused depth requires a suitable parallel-view stereoscope or viewing technique; ordinary screens show two distinct images. A single photograph is kept flat.
Reduced motion disables automatic progression and transition motion. Offscreen, hidden-tab and Lab pause states suspend animation and mute audio. Audio only starts after pressing Enable click sound.
Local image files are decoded at up to 1,800 pixels on their longest edge. Up to 24 scenes per reel. Built-in scenes redraw only on interaction or during a short transition; no idle render loop.
notes: Elsewhere is an original pocket-viewer design: molded plastic, inset binocular lenses, a geared shutter lever and a cream circular reel. No protected product artwork or branding is reproduced.

Six illustrated scenes and six miniature-world scenes use shared projected geometry. The left and right eyes converge on the same central plane; closer and farther structures create different binocular disparities.
The photo reel includes three credited photographs. Local images remain flat; true stereo pairs can be supplied through the reel schema. No depth inference or remote processing occurs.

Each scene has two reel windows. The selected pair rotates toward the viewing slot; a brief shutter closes while the scene changes. Reordering creates a custom reel without modifying the sample collections.
The optional click is a quiet procedural Web Audio impulse triggered by manual advances. A restored sound setting never unlocks audio without an explicit gesture.
reuse: Download the complete source ZIP or use pnpm lab:export view-master. It includes original code, all sample assets and their credits, an offline-capable standalone example, and a custom-reel integration example.

model.js owns validation, settings and transport. reels.js contains sample content. renderer.js owns scene projection and image drawing. audio.js provides optional clicks; index.js and styles.js provide the toy shell.

Call mount(container, settings, report, { reel, onSceneChange }). Supply illustrated scenes, miniature worlds, photographs or registered left/right stereo pairs. README.md documents the versioned schema.
The returned API provides update, setRunning, replay, loadReel, getState, exportReel and dispose. Dispose when removing the viewer to release listeners, image caches, observers and audio resources.
Lab presets and source exports save settings, not visitors’ private photographs. Save this reel exports an explicit portable JSON with embedded images and the chosen order.
